elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that Vendor-supplied services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires Array to defend the Ono Indemnitees, which include Ono and its Affiliates, against Third Party Claims alleging that a Product, deliverable, or service supplied by Array infringes or misappropriates third-party IP rights.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that Vendor-supplied services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly requires Array to indemnify the Ono Indemnitees against the specified third-party IP claims.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2's chapeau imposes a defense duty for all listed triggers, and subsection (e) covers Array's breach of applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2 expressly indemnifies the Ono Indemnitees for Third Party Claims arising from Array's breach of applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2(f) reaches only unauthorized access to or disclosure of Ono's Confidential Information caused by Array. It does not cover the full data-breach category, such as loss, destruction, alteration, or breaches involving other Customer-controlled or protected data.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The indemnity is limited to unauthorized access to or disclosure of Ono's Confidential Information and therefore is narrower than an indemnity for any data breach caused by Array.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2's defense obligation applies to subsection (g), which expressly includes Array's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2(g) expressly covers Third Party Claims arising from Array's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2's defense obligation applies to subsection (g), which expressly includes Array's willful misconduct.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2(g) expressly covers Third Party Claims arising from Array's willful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require prompt written notice of a covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3 requires the Indemnitee to promptly notify the Indemnitor in writing and limits relief for late notice to circumstances involving prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the Indemnitor control of the defense and settlement of a covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3 gives the Indemnitor sole control of the defense and/or settlement, subject to status updates and consideration of the Indemnitee's reasonable comments.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the Indemnitee to cooperate with the Indemnitor in defending a covered third-party claim.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3 requires the Indemnitee to cooperate fully with the Indemnitor and its legal representatives in the investigation of a covered claim.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from content provided by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 16.1(a) covers materials, data, or content provided by Ono to Array under the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 16.1(b) covers Ono's breach of applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must contain no affirmative trigger other than Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The redlined Section 16.1 contains only the supplied-materials/data/content trigger and the applicable-law trigger. The misconduct language is an exclusion rather than an additional indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that Vendor-supplied services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly indemnifies the Ono Indemnitees against Third Party Claims alleging that a Product, deliverable, or service supplied by Array infringes or misappropriates third-party IP rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer's modification of the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combining the services or deliverables with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from compliance with Customer-provided specifications or instructions.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications or instructions exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have an operative remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no procurement-of-rights remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have an operative remedy to modify the affected item so that it becomes non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have an operative remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have an operative refund remedy if procurement, modification, or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times the annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the rendered clause. The reference to Section 11.4 does not establish such a cap in the supplied language.

result.reason: The redline supplies most of the preferred allocation, including defense and indemnity for IP, legal breach, gross negligence, and willful misconduct; standard claim procedures; and a narrowed Customer indemnity. It fails the preferred position because the data-security trigger is limited to unauthorized access to or disclosure of Ono's Confidential Information rather than all data breaches caused by Array. It fails the fallback because all customary IP exclusions and remedies and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The drafting also retains broken subsection numbering, places the IP obligation after the procedural text without a separate subsection, and contains the grammatical error 'a Ono Indemnitee.'
